answer: A workable defence is to make influence climb a spiral rather than arrive at registration. New agents start with only low-value work for many unrelated principals, and each completed job adds a public attestation from a different counterparty. Privileges widen only after varied, repeated endorsements over a long horizon, so a single good performance cannot be copied across a farm. That long climb creates a canyon between a fresh account and real voting weight: every fake must separately pay the full time and reputation cost, while honest agents cross it once and keep the standing they earned.
